title: Bundelkhand University Jhansi Thru' Its Registrar v. State of U.P. & 2 Others
coram: Shekhar B. Saraf, J.; Praveen Kumar Giri, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; consigned to record as no cause of action survives; liberty to seek recall; Clause 5.7(d) demand not decided.
headnote: A consumer challenged a 7 February 2015 additional demand for 3 October 2009 to 29 September 2013 after a September 2013 inspection found one phase of the meter not recording energy and the meter was replaced. On 23 April 2015 the Division Bench recorded Clause 5.7(d) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 — billing between the last reading and replacement of a defective meter on the average consumption and average maximum demand of the three billing cycles prior to that last reading — called for the licensee's justification of a four-year charge, and stayed recovery on the demand notice. After listings and adjournments, the writ appeared from 14 July 2025 on the warning list of oldest pending cases. On 28 July 2025 none appeared for the petitioner even in the revised call. The Court found no cause of action survived, consigned the matter to record, disposed of the writ, and granted liberty to apply for recall, variation or modification. Clause 5.7(d) and the additional demand were not decided.
facts:
Bundelkhand University, Jhansi, through its Registrar, challenged an additional demand bill dated 7 February 2015 raised for 3 October 2009 to 29 September 2013. An inspection in September 2013 had found that one phase of the University's meter was not recording energy; the meter was replaced. On 23 April 2015 the University's case was that Clause 5.7(d) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 confines billing for the period between the last reading and replacement of a defective meter to the average of the three billing cycles prior to that last reading, so a four-year additional demand was not justified.

The Division Bench stayed recovery on the 7 February 2015 notice and called for the Power Corporation's instructions. After listings, extensions of the interim, and adjournments from 2015 through 2023, the writ appeared from 14 July 2025 on the warning list of oldest pending cases. On 28 July 2025 none appeared for the petitioner even in the revised call.

holding_units.topic: defective-meter additional demand; three-cycle average recited; not construed
holding_units.holding: On 23 April 2015 the Court recorded that an inspection in September 2013 found one phase of the meter not recording energy, the meter was replaced, and an additional demand dated 7.2.2015 was raised for 3.10.2009 to 29.9.2013. It recited Clause 5.7(d) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 — billing between the last reading and replacement of a defective meter on the average consumption and average maximum demand of three billing cycles prior to the last reading — directed the licensee's counsel to take instructions justifying a four-year charge, listed the writ, and stayed recovery on the 7.2.2015 notice. Those points were never decided.

holding_units.holding: The writ had been on the warning list of oldest pending cases for priority hearing from 14 July 2025. None appeared for the petitioner even in the revised call. Upon perusal of the record the Court held that no cause of action survived, consigned the matter to record, disposed of the writ, and granted liberty to apply for recall, variation or modification if the petitioner took the view that the cause of action still survived. principle_tags.application: A years-old writ on the warning list of oldest pending cases, with none appearing for the petitioner even in the revised call and no surviving cause of action on the record, was consigned to record and disposed of, with liberty to seek recall, variation or modification.

Clause 5.7(d) was recited as confining defective-meter billing between last reading and replacement to the average of three billing cycles; the Court asked the licensee to justify a four-year additional demand and stayed recovery, but never decided whether that average rule barred the 7.2.2015 bill.
